reason: This is the only available combination, and the calcium signal appears to be the next step toward a pull.
expectation: I expect calcium to uncover the binding site and allow the filaments to interact, though I’m unsure how much of the pull the result will show.

effect: Calcium exposes the grip sites, allowing myosin to cycle and slide the filaments past one another; the fibre shortens without the filaments themselves shortening.
reaction: The two poses make the distinction between sliding and filament shortening clear.
reason: This is the only available combination, and pumping calcium back into storage should help the fibre relax.
expectation: I expect the membranes to use ATP to return calcium to storage, allowing the binding sites to be covered again and the fibre to relax.

effect: Calcium pumps use ATP to restore calcium to storage, covering the grip sites and stopping pulling; an outside pull then helps the fibre relax.
reaction: It was interesting that relaxation also requires cellular work.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding the calcium signal was most worthwhile: the description connected the molecular action to the fibre shortening and explained that the filaments slide rather than shorten.

leastWorthwhile.text: Building the fibre and filling it with filaments felt repetitive because each was the only available combination and the results mostly set up later events.

surprise.text: I was surprised that ATP helps myosin release and reset, and that calcium pumping also needs ATP during relaxation.

arbitrary.text: No action felt clearly arbitrary, although combining the transporter-bearing cell with muscle fibre structures produced a scaffold without much explanation of how they fit together.

continue.text: I would continue for another chapter to see how the muscle fibre connects to larger body systems. The later close-ups made the cellular work more interesting than the early assembly steps.
